mobile-money-agent.intro: Mobile money is the financial backbone of West Africa. Learn to run a kiosk professionally — transactions, fraud prevention, customer service, and the business skills to build a super-agent operation.

skillDomains.name: Transaction Fundamentals
skillDomains.description: Handle cash and mobile transactions with accuracy and confidence.

skills.name: Cash Handling
skills.description: Manage physical cash, count accurately, prevent loss.

modules.title: Cash is trust
modules.content:
Your customers trust you with their money. Every transaction is a small moment of that trust being tested.

Golden rules of cash handling

  • Count cash in front of the customer, twice
  • State the amount out loud: "I'm giving you 45,000 Le."
  • Use a calculator for every transaction, even simple ones
  • Never mix personal money with business cash
  • Never serve customers while distracted or rushed

A single moment of careless handling can lose a customer forever — or cost you your float.

modules.title: Counting techniques
modules.content:
Cash in

  1. Receive the money
  2. State the amount out loud
  3. Count twice — once fast, once slow
  4. Confirm with the customer before entering the transaction
  5. Enter the amount into the system
  6. Give a printed or SMS receipt

Cash out

  1. Confirm the transaction on the system first
  2. Count the cash twice
  3. State the amount as you hand it over
  4. Wait for the customer to count
  5. Only then say goodbye

steps.q: A customer is in a hurry and says 'just give me the money, I'll count later'. What do you do?
o: Insist on counting together before they leave
Give a bit less to be safe
steps.f: Counting together protects both of you.

steps.q: You notice your float is 5,000 Le short at end of day. What do you do?
o: Top up from personal money and forget
Review the day's transactions to find the error, log the shortage
steps.f: Find the error honestly. Log it.

steps.q: A regular customer asks you to 'hold' 30,000 Le for them until tomorrow. What do you do?
o: Decline — this is not an authorised service and breaks rules
Hold it but don't tell anyone
steps.f: Holding cash for customers is not part of your mandate.

skills.name: Float Management
skills.description: Keep enough cash and e-money to serve customers all day.

modules.title: The two-sided float
modules.content:
You manage two balances:

  • Physical cash — the notes in your drawer
  • E-money — the digital balance in your agent account

Every transaction moves value between the two:

  • Cash-in (customer deposits): you receive cash, you send e-money → cash goes up, e-money goes down
  • Cash-out (customer withdraws): you give cash, you receive e-money → cash goes down, e-money goes up

If either runs out, you can't serve customers. Managing both is your daily job.

modules.title: Planning your float
modules.content:
Track your patterns

Over a week you'll learn:

  • Mondays and Fridays are busiest (market days)
  • Month-end is heavy (salary payments)
  • Evenings are cash-out heavy (people going home)
  • Mornings are cash-in heavy (traders depositing)

Rules of thumb

  • Keep 3× your average hourly cash out during peak hours
  • Top up e-money before month-end
  • Visit the super-agent twice a week minimum
  • Never let either balance drop below 20% of your peak-hour needs

modules.title: Handle a float crisis
modules.prompt: It's Friday at 5 PM — market closing time. You've just done your 15th cash-out of the hour. Your physical cash is down to 8,000 Le but customers keep arriving. Your super-agent is 20 minutes away and closes at 6 PM. What do you do?
modules.context: Float management is a real skill tested in moments like this.

skills.name: System Operations
skills.description: Use the mobile money platform fluently and safely.

modules.title: Know your platform inside out
modules.content:
Every mobile money platform has the same core operations:

  • Customer registration
  • Cash-in (deposit)
  • Cash-out (withdrawal)
  • Transfer (customer to customer)
  • Balance check
  • Transaction reversal (rare, controlled)

Speed comes from repetition. But speed without accuracy is dangerous.

steps.q: A customer wants to send 50,000 Le to their son in another city. Which operation?
steps.f: Sending to another person is a transfer.

steps.q: The system shows a transaction success but the customer says they didn't receive the SMS. What do you do?
o: Check the system record and print/screenshot the confirmation
steps.f: Verify in the system. The SMS may be delayed.

steps.q: A customer says they made a mistake and wants a reversal. What do you do?
o: Explain that reversals require customer care procedures and direct them to the helpline
steps.f: Agents do not reverse transactions unilaterally.

skillDomains.name: Fraud Awareness
skillDomains.description: Recognise scams before they hit your customers — or you.

skills.name: Common Scams
skills.description: Know the patterns of fraud targeting mobile money agents.

modules.title: The five scams you'll see
modules.content:
1. Fake SMS confirmation

Customer shows a fake SMS saying 'payment received' but no money is in your account. Always verify on your system, never on their phone.

2. Reversed transaction trick

Customer initiates a transaction then reverses it after you've given cash. Wait for confirmed success, not just pending.

3. Distraction theft

One person distracts while another takes cash. Watch your float, always.

4. Fake agent impersonation

Someone claims to be from the network provider asking for your PIN or balance. Real providers NEVER ask for these.

5. Overpayment scam

Customer 'accidentally' sends too much and asks for a cash refund of the difference. The original payment then reverses.

steps.q: A caller says they're from the network head office and asks you to read your agent PIN to verify your account. What do you do?
o: Refuse and hang up — real providers never ask for PINs
steps.f: No legitimate provider will ever ask for your PIN.

steps.q: A customer shows an SMS saying 'You have received 45,000 Le' and wants cash. Your system doesn't show the credit. What do you do?
o: Give cash anyway — SMS says so
Refuse — SMS is fake or delayed, verify on the system
steps.f: The system is the source of truth.

steps.q: A customer sends 100,000 Le instead of 10,000 Le and asks for 90,000 Le refund in cash. What do you do?
o: Refuse — reverse the transaction through proper channels only
steps.f: The overpayment scam relies on the original transaction being reversed later.

modules.context: Fraud prevention sometimes means refusing service.

skillDomains.name: Customer Service
skillDomains.description: Great service brings customers back. Bad service loses them forever.

skills.name: Communication
skills.description: Explain, listen, and manage every kind of customer.

modules.title: How to talk to every customer
modules.content:
Three customer types

  • The confused first-timer — needs patience and simple language
  • The regular in a hurry — needs speed and recognition
  • The frustrated one — needs listening before solving

Universal rules

  • Greet by name when you know it
  • Make eye contact
  • Explain what you're doing as you do it
  • Never argue. If you're wrong, apologise. If they're wrong, stay calm.
  • Thank them at the end, every time

steps.q: An elderly customer doesn't understand what 'e-money' means. What do you do?
o: Use a simple analogy ("it's like a phone-based bank account")
steps.f: Simple analogies work. Meet the customer at their level.

steps.q: A customer shouts at you because their transaction failed (not your fault). What do you do?
o: Listen calmly, apologise for the inconvenience, help solve it
steps.f: Anger is usually about the situation, not you.

steps.q: A customer asks you to break a 10,000 Le note into smaller ones — no transaction. What do you do?
o: Help if you can — it builds loyalty

skills.name: Financial Inclusion
skills.description: Serve people the traditional banks ignored. This is your mission.

modules.title: You are the bank for millions
modules.content:
Across West Africa, mobile money is the primary financial service for most adults. Your kiosk may be someone's only access to savings, transfers, or bill payments.

This is not just a job — it is a public service.

Special responsibilities

  • Treat small transactions with the same respect as large ones
  • Help customers understand fees and balances
  • Encourage savings habits
  • Never shame a customer for a small amount

modules.title: Design a financial inclusion initiative
modules.prompt: Design a simple program to help unbanked people in your community use mobile money. It could be a savings club, a bill-payment workshop, or a registration drive for the elderly.
steps: Identify a specific group not using mobile money
Understand why (trust, confusion, no phone, no ID)
Design a program that removes those barriers
Write it as a one-page proposal

skillDomains.name: Business Operations
skillDomains.description: Run your kiosk as a business, not a favour.

skills.name: Record Keeping
skills.description: Track every transaction and balance for accuracy and trust.

modules.title: Why records matter
modules.content:
Your daily records are the difference between an agent and a professional. Track:

  • Every transaction (time, type, amount, customer)
  • Opening and closing float (cash + e-money)
  • Shortages or surpluses
  • Disputes and how they were resolved

Tools

  • Notebook and pen — works everywhere, always
  • Simple spreadsheet on your phone
  • The provider's agent app — has its own transaction log

At day's end, reconcile. Opening balance + transactions = closing balance. If not, find out why.

steps.q: Your opening balance is 500,000 Le. During the day you received 300,000 in cash-in and paid out 420,000 in cash-out. What should your closing cash be?
At close, your physical cash is 375,000 Le but records say 380,000 Le. What do you do?
o: Note the 5,000 Le shortage and review the day's transactions

steps.q: A customer disputes a transaction from last week. What's your best defence?
o: Your daily transaction log with time, amount, and receipt number

skills.name: Growing Your Business
skills.description: Move from one kiosk to a small network.

modules.title: From agent to super-agent
modules.content:
Every large agent network started with one kiosk. Growth path:

  1. Single kiosk — you serve customers directly
  2. Two or three kiosks — you hire assistants
  3. Sub-agents — smaller agents under you for float
  4. Super-agent — you serve other agents' float needs

What enables growth

  • Consistent reliability (never out of float)
  • Excellent service (customers return)
  • Clean records (providers trust you)
  • Location (foot traffic + safety)

modules.title: Plan your second kiosk
modules.prompt: Your first kiosk is doing well — 400 transactions a week and steady profit. You want to open a second location. Describe how you'd choose the location and manage both.
modules.context: Growth without systems is chaos. Plan before expanding.
rubric: Chooses location based on foot traffic and safety
Considers distance from first kiosk (don't cannibalise)
Plans for staff (trusted family member or trained employee)
Sets up separate float management for each location
Sets a financial review period (3 months) to judge success

modules.title: Write a one-year growth plan
modules.prompt: Write a one-page business plan for growing your mobile money business over the next 12 months. Include: target transactions per week, locations, staffing, and financial projections.
steps: Estimate costs and revenue per month
